newsitem.title: SPAIN: Greenpeace asks Spain to abandon Morocco cable.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace asks Spain to abandon Morocco cable.

text.p: Greenpeace asked Spain on Wednesday to halt work on a high-tension power line to Morocco which has sparked protests in a southern Spanish coastal town.

Nine people were lightly injured on Monday in Tarifa, where clashes erupted between police and protesters opposed to the laying of the cable. Tarifa's municipality ordered a suspension of work after the clashes.
Greenpeace said Spain was seeking to export its excess electricity to Morocco rather than cut back production of "dirty" energy from coal and nuclear plants.

"Greenpeace considers the high-tension line between Spain and Morocco absolutely unnecessary for the energy policies of both countries," the international environment group said in an appeal to the Spanish government.
Protests against the cable have erupted periodically in Tarifa, on Spain's tourist-crammed southern coast.
Red Electrica Espanola, the company constructing the power line across the Straits of Gibraltar to link Spanish and Moroccan grids, decided last year to alter the route after protests in Tarifa.
Red Electrica could not be reached for comment on Wednesday about the municipality's decision to suspend construction and it was not immediately clear whether the project would continue.
Greenpeace urged the government to develop cleaner sources of energy and said the power cable to Morocco would only encourage waste and discourage use of alternative energy sources.
The group proposed the government immediately begin phasing out nuclear and fossil fuel plants.
